newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs soar at close on economic package hope.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs soar at close on economic package hope.

text.p: Anticipation of government economic boosting measures sparked across-the-board buying interest on Monday, sending the stock market to close sharply higher, brokers said.
The Finance and Economic Ministry is scheduled to announce new economic package on Thursday, which investors believe will be aimed at reviving the nation's sagging economy.
"Investors are pinning their hopes on the looming government announcement," said Park Key-pyong of Hanyang Securities.
The composite stock index soared 2.66 percent or 17.07 points to 658.90.
Analysts said the economic package was expected to include measures to stabilise rising interest rate and the weak domestic currency, and to revamp the real name financial system.

"Investors believe the package will contain an expansion of foreign stock ownership ceiling," said analyst Kim Wan-hee of Dongsuh Securities. "The hope is pushing up blue chips as they are expected to be major beneficiaries of a higher ceiling."

After the market close, a finance and economic ministry official told Reuters the government was considering expanding the foreign stock ownership limit to above the earlier planned 23 percent in 1997. At present, the ceiling is 20 percent.
Samsung Electronics rose 2,000 won to 55,000 and POSCO gained 2,300 won to 43,000.
Brokers said the market was about to rebound technically following steep falls last week. Out of 702 rising shares, 128 went limit up.
"The issue of the economic measures is not likely to continue to support gains as sharp as shown today. But it will limit steep falls at least until Thursday," Park said.
Expectation of inflowing money from on-shore funds set up by investment trust companies also boosted the market, brokers said. -- YEOM YOON-JEONG (822) 727 5647
